r0.why: Byzantium colony 7th c BC (23), Megara c.657 BC opposite Chalcedon (38), Darius 512 BC narrowest point/pontoon bridge (39), c.150 BC treaty tribute for independence (41), nearly three centuries of peaceful prosperity (42)

r1.why: Not like Athens/Sparta but prosperous trading city (43); land route, Black Sea-Mediterranean seaway, Golden Horn harbour (44); palaces/domes/towers from prosperity as gateway between two continents and two seas (13)

r2.why: Founded/refounded 324 under Constantine as Nova Roma (4,26,38); eastern capital 330 and sole capital after 5th-c loss of west (5); built to rival Rome with seven-hill claim (12); name Constantinople = city of Constantine (28)

r3.why: Largest and wealthiest in Europe mid-5th to early 13th c (7); Hagia Sophia, palace, Hippodrome, Golden Gate (8); 5th-c university, library >100,000 volumes (9); called 'the City' by citizens and provincials, source of Istanbul (30,31)

r4.why: Golden Horn and Marmara reduced land needing walls (11); Theodosian double wall ~2 km west with moat and palisades (10); impenetrable nearly 900 years despite many sieges (14)

r5.why: 1204 sack and Latin Empire (15); Nicaea recapture 1261 (16); shrinking with Ottoman rise (18); early 15th c reduced to city, environs, Morea (19); 1453 conquest (20); capital until 1923, moved to Ankara (21); Istanbul most populous, >16 million (22)
